root_idea.summary: The root denotes aversion, hatred, and what stands opposite to love.
root_idea.development: Its central orientation is the soul's turning away from something unwanted, contrasted with love as attraction toward what is desired. Classical usage develops this orientation into states of being hateful, causing hatred, reciprocal hatred, and descriptions of hated or hating persons.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic nominal citation form بَغْضَاءُ.

senses.definition: Hatred or aversion; the opposite of love.
senses.usage_conditions: A noun for hostile aversion or hatred. In the Quran it is coordinated with العداوة in some passages and may describe hostility that becomes manifest in speech or relations between groups.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become hateful, odious, or an object of hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I; the source also records variant vocalizations of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's fortune or good fortune to fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical idiom, especially associated with Yemeni usage; also used as an imprecation concerning another person's fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone hateful, odious, or an object of hatred to others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II, causative; it is contrasted with making someone beloved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hate reciprocally, or to engage in vehement mutual hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III; used for reciprocal hostility between two parties.
Form IV, transitive. The supplied lexical discussion also compares this form with dialectal analyses of other expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: How hateful or odious he is to me.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression of wonder; related prepositional patterns can express the relation of hating or being hated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: May the eye of your enemy be pained by the sight of what he hates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical imprecatory expression; the exact verbal form and interpretation vary in the reported formulations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To manifest or show hatred; to become or make oneself an object of hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V; contrasted with showing love or making oneself beloved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hate one another; to be mutually hateful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VI, describing reciprocal hatred among members of a group or between parties.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hatred; بِغْضَةٌ and بَغَاضَةٌ may denote vehement hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal derivatives for the state or quality of hatred; the intensity expressed by the latter variants is a lexical nuance of the same semantic branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hateful, odious, hated, or an object of hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival and passive descriptions of one who or something that is hated. The related plural بُغَضَاءُ is also reported. One cited interpretation gives بَغِيضٌ the contrary sense “hating.”
Active-participial usage, associated in the lexical discussion with the reported contrary interpretation of بَغِيضٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or occasion of hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of place or circumstance denoting what gives rise to hatred.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit records both the ordinary hated/odious sense and a reported contrary hating sense.

cautions: The adjective بَغِيضٌ is reported with both the ordinary sense “hated” and a contrary sense “hating”; these readings are kept explicit rather than silently conflated.
A Quran citation occurs in the Form IV lexical discussion, but no modern verse example is assigned to it here because the supplied QAC form group contains only the nominal form بَغْضَاءُ.
